text:
ana: Quick follow-up from the gateway spike: we need a clear operational playbook for reclaiming streaming slots. Two main options surfaced: passive-evict (mark & wait for client retry) vs active-reclaim (send trailer + release resources immediately). Want to capture tradeoffs.

peter: Passive-evict is safer for semantics (less surprise for clients) but holds memory longer. Active-reclaim is better for tight pools but requires clear client contract and retry hints.

kevin: Additional dimension: charging semantics. If we cut a stream mid-output, how do we report billing? Marking as "aborted_partial" and emitting tokens_used in logs seems simplest. We must avoid double-billing when client retries.

shreya: From infra: we don't currently surface a per-stream estimate to admission control. Proposed cheap counters: tokenized_context_bytes, buffered_chunks_bytes, kv_estimate_mb. Update per write. Admission sums these to decide.

ana: I'd like to formalize the trailer contract for active-reclaim. Minimal required fields: `reclaim-id`, `reason`, `policy`, `estimated_saved_mb`, `partial=true|false`, `retry-after-ms` (optional). Example: ```json
{"reclaim-id":"r-1234","reason":"idle","policy":"soft","estimated_saved_mb":"12","partial":"true","retry-after-ms":"1500"}
```

peter: Also include a `sideeffect-safe` flag to indicate whether any function/tool calls were confirmed. If false -> callers must not act on deltas.

kevin: For hedging+early-fallback: hedged attempts should be netted out in billing only once when the one that returns first yields tokens. But if reclaim forces a retry, we bill each attempt's consumed tokens. Document this edge case.

ops-bot: RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/289 - added "stream-reclaim" appendix. CI: load tests failing on reclaim path. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

shreya: We should expose an opt-in client header to request "preserve" semantics: `x-rw-preserve-stream: duration=ms`. If set, gateway will avoid reclaiming that stream up to the duration but will still account toward pool budget. For Dedicated pools we can ignore opt-in unless admin enabled.

ana: Proposed config knobs to land behind ff:
```
ingress:
  reclaim:
    idle_ms: 750
    mode: active   # active | passive
    reserve_mb_per_conn: 1
    preserve_opt_in: false
```

peter: Test coverage: (A) chaos: random reclaim during streaming with function-call payloads and assert no side-effect leak, (B) billing probe: reclaimed attempts produce partial billing event, (C) SDK: how to handle `reclaim-id` and `retry-after`.

kevin: Observability: emit `stream.reclaim.count` with tags: reason, mode, pool, tenant; and `stream.reclaim.latency_ms` for time between last-chunk and reclaim. Also sample full trace with `reclaim-id`.

shreya: Implementation plan: 1) admission: add stream footprint counters (PR), 2) runtime: trailer emitter + reclaim state machine (PR), 3) billing: partial/billed tokens marker + link to reclaim-id (finance PR), 4) sdk docs + sample retry logic (devex). I'll own runtime work.

ana: One safety rule: never active-reclaim within first N ms of a stream (warmup) to avoid hurting interactive clients. Default warmup=250ms.

ops-bot: TODO created: INF-4123 (admission counters), INF-4124 (reclaim trailers), INF-4125 (billing markers).

peter: Let's ship a spike behind feature-flag in Dedicated first and run it for one pool. Close monitoring dashboard and explicit kill-switch.

ana: OK I'll draft the RFC appendix wording and trailer schema. Will include examples for function-call flows and a tiny SDK snippet showing how to detect `reclaim-id` and `retry-after-ms`.

kevin: Final call: prefer passive for PLG default, active for constrained pools. Document tradeoffs clearly.

shreya: Agreed. I'll land runtime counters this week and iterate.
